flows.name: Visit landing page and get started
flows.start: On the public landing page (not signed in)
flows.goal: Understand what DashForge is for and start creating dashboards.

steps.userAction: The visitor views the public landing page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows what DashForge is for — a single personal space for notes, numbers, tasks and links — with a preview of the dark glowing console style with neon controls, edges, numbers, monospace figures and faint grid behind widgets, and a clear Create / Get Started call to action to sign up or sign in.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to get started to create an account.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-up form.

alternatives.condition: The visitor already has an account and chooses to sign in instead.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-in form.

flows.outcome: Visitor has seen what DashForge does, the dark glowing console preview, and has a clear path to sign up or sign in.

flows.name: Sign up
flows.start: On the landing page
flows.goal: Create a private account to own dashboards.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-up form.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the account, signs the user in with a persistent session and shows the home dashboard list.

alternatives.condition: The email is not a valid email address, or the password is shorter than 8 characters or longer than 128 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that is wrong, explains what is required and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: The email already has an account.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says an account with that email already exists and offers to sign in instead.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-in form.

alternatives.condition: Creating the account fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the values and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: Account created, user is signed in with persistent session and taken to their dashboard list (home); refresh keeps them signed in.

flows.name: Sign in
flows.start: On the landing page
flows.goal: Sign in to access private dashboards.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-in form.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website verifies the credentials, restores the persistent session and shows the home dashboard list sorted by last edited most recent first.

alternatives.condition: The email is not a valid email address or the password is empty.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that is wrong, explains what is required and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: The email and password do not match any account.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the email or password is incorrect and keeps the email while clearing the password.

alternatives.condition: Signing in fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the values and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: User is signed in with persistent session and sees their dashboard list; refresh keeps them signed in.

flows.name: Sign out
flows.start: On any signed-in page (home or editor)
flows.goal: End the session securely.

steps.userAction: The user chooses to sign out.
steps.websiteResponse: The website ends the persistent session and shows the public landing page.

alternatives.condition: Signing out fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the user signed in and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: Session ended, user is returned to the public landing page; dashboards are no longer accessible until sign in again.

flows.name: See my dashboards (home)
flows.start: After signing in or navigating to home
flows.goal: See all my dashboards last-edited first and open one or create a new one.

steps.userAction: The user navigates to home.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the list of the user's dashboards sorted by last edited most recent first, each showing dashboard name and when it was last edited as relative time with full timestamp on hover, and a search field to filter by name and an action to create a new dashboard.

steps.userAction: The user chooses a dashboard from the list to open it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website opens that dashboard in the editor.

alternatives.condition: The user has no dashboards yet.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty state message that no dashboards exist yet and invites the user to create the first dashboard via the Create dashboard action that starts creating a new dashboard.

alternatives.condition: The user filters dashboards by name.

steps.userAction: The user types in the search field to filter dashboards by name.
steps.websiteResponse: The website filters the list to only dashboards whose name contains the typed text and shows the matching results.

alternatives.condition: No dashboard name matches the search text.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that no results match the search and offers to clear the search to see all dashboards again.

steps.userAction: The user clears the search.
steps.websiteResponse: The website restores the full list of dashboards sorted by last edited most recent first.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is no longer available and shows the home list again.

flows.outcome: User sees the list of their dashboards with name and last edited time, sorted most recent first; empty state invites creating first dashboard; refresh shows same list.

flows.name: Open dashboard in editor
flows.start: On the home dashboard list
flows.goal: Open a dashboard to view and work with its widgets.

steps.userAction: The user selects a dashboard from the list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website opens the editor for that Dashboard showing its name, Saving/Saved status, and its Widgets in relative order in the glowing console grid.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the home dashboard list.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard has no widgets yet.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the editor with the dashboard name and Saving/Saved status and an empty state inviting the user to add a widget.

flows.outcome: Dashboard editor is open showing dashboard name, Saving/Saved status, and its ordered widgets in the glowing console grid; refresh restores same state.

flows.name: Create a new dashboard
flows.start: On the home dashboard list or from the editor
flows.goal: Start a new empty dashboard and begin editing immediately.

steps.userAction: The user chooses to create a dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates a new Dashboard with default name Untitled Dashboard (numbered if needed), sets lastEditedAt to now with no widgets, and opens it in the editor showing its name and Saving/Saved status.

alternatives.condition: Creating the dashboard fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the user where they were and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: New Dashboard created with default name Untitled Dashboard (numbered if needed) and empty widget list, opened in editor; it appears in the home list sorted by lastEditedAt descending; refresh keeps it.

flows.name: Rename dashboard
flows.start: In the dashboard editor or from the home list row action
flows.goal: Change the dashboard's name.
preconditions: At least one dashboard exists and is open or listed.

steps.userAction: The user chooses to rename the dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard name field with the current name ready to edit.

steps.userAction: The user edits the name and confirms.
steps.websiteResponse: The website validates the name, auto-saves with Saving then Saved status, updates lastEditedAt, and shows the new name in the editor and home list.

alternatives.condition: The name is empty or longer than 80 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the name field as invalid, explains it is required and max 80 characters, and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving the new name fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed name and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the home dashboard list.

alternatives.condition: The user cancels renaming.

steps.websiteResponse: Nothing is changed; the website shows the dashboard with its previous name.

flows.outcome: Dashboard name (FD03) updated, lastEditedAt refreshed, auto-saved with Saved status; new name appears in editor and home list and survives refresh.

flows.name: Duplicate dashboard
flows.start: On the home dashboard list or in the dashboard editor
flows.goal: Make a copy of a dashboard with all widgets to start a new one from it.

steps.userAction: The user chooses Duplicate on a dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates a copy named '{original name} Copy' with all Widgets, their order, sizes, titles and content copied exactly, sets lastEditedAt to now, shows it in the home list sorted by lastEditedAt descending and opens it in the editor.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the home dashboard list.

alternatives.condition: Duplicating the dashboard fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the original dashboard unchanged and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: New Dashboard created named '{original name} Copy' with all Widgets, their order, sizes, titles and content copied exactly, with fresh lastEditedAt and shown in the home list sorted by lastEditedAt descending; refresh keeps both.

flows.name: Delete dashboard
flows.start: On the home dashboard list or in the dashboard editor
flows.goal: Permanently remove a dashboard and its widgets.

steps.userAction: The user chooses Delete on a dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks the user to confirm permanently deleting the dashboard and all its widgets.

alternatives.condition: The user confirms the deletion.

steps.websiteResponse: The website permanently deletes the dashboard and all its widgets, removes it from the home list, and if the user was in the editor returns them to the home list.

alternatives.condition: The user cancels.

steps.websiteResponse: Nothing is deleted; the website shows the dashboard as it was.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was already deleted.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is already gone and shows the home dashboard list.

alternatives.condition: Deleting fails after confirmation.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the dashboard and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: Dashboard and all its Widgets permanently deleted, removed from home list; if deleted from editor user returns to home; refresh keeps it gone.

flows.name: Add a widget to dashboard
flows.start: In the dashboard editor
flows.goal: Add a new note, counter, checklist or link list block to the dashboard.
preconditions: A dashboard is open in the editor.

steps.userAction: The user chooses to add a widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the widget create form with type, title and size.

steps.userAction: The user picks a widget type, optionally edits the title and size, and submits.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the widget with the chosen type, title defaulting to capitalized type name if left empty, size defaulting to medium, assigns it the next order position with type-specific defaults (note text empty, counter 0 with empty label, checklist empty, link list empty), shows it in the grid, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

alternatives.condition: The title is longer than 60 characters or no type is selected.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that is wrong, explains the limit, and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Creating the widget fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The user cancels adding the widget.

steps.websiteResponse: Nothing is created; the website shows the editor as it was.

flows.outcome: New Widget created with chosen type, default title, size medium, appended in order; auto-saved and lastEditedAt updated; refresh keeps it.

flows.name: Configure widget title
flows.start: In the dashboard editor on an existing widget
flows.goal: Change a widget's title.
preconditions: Dashboard open with at least one widget.

steps.userAction: The user opens the title for editing on the widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the widget title field editable with the current title or the default type name.

steps.userAction: The user edits the title and confirms.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new title, shows Saving then Saved, updates lastEditedAt, and shows the updated title on the widget.

alternatives.condition: The title is longer than 60 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the title field, explains the 60 character limit, and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving the title fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed title and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The widget was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the widget is gone and shows the editor without it.

flows.outcome: Widget title updated, auto-saved, lastEditedAt refreshed; change survives refresh.

flows.name: Reposition widget
flows.start: In the dashboard editor on an existing widget
flows.goal: Change the widget's position relative to other widgets.
preconditions: Dashboard open with at least one widget.

steps.userAction: The user moves the widget to a new position using up/down controls or drag handle.
steps.websiteResponse: The website updates the widget's order index, re-renders the grid in the new relative order, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

alternatives.condition: Saving the new order fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the previous order, shows that saving failed, and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The widget was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the widget is gone and shows the editor without it.

alternatives.condition: There is only one widget so there is nowhere to move.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the widget in place and indicates that reordering needs at least two widgets.

flows.outcome: Widget order updated, new relative order rendered in grid, auto-saved and lastEditedAt refreshed; order survives refresh.

flows.name: Resize widget
flows.start: In the dashboard editor on an existing widget
flows.goal: Change the widget's visual footprint between small, medium and large.
preconditions: Dashboard open with at least one widget.

steps.userAction: The user opens the size control on the widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the size options small, medium and large with the current size selected.

steps.userAction: The user picks a size.
steps.websiteResponse: The website applies the new visual footprint to the widget, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

alternatives.condition: Saving the new size fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the previous size, shows that saving failed, and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The widget was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the widget is gone and shows the editor without it.

flows.outcome: Widget size updated to small/medium/large, visual footprint changes, auto-saved and lastEditedAt refreshed; size survives refresh.

flows.name: Remove widget
flows.start: In the dashboard editor on an existing widget
flows.goal: Permanently remove a widget and its contents from the dashboard.
preconditions: Dashboard open with at least one widget.

steps.userAction: The user chooses Remove on the widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks the user to confirm permanently deleting the widget and its contents.

alternatives.condition: The user confirms the deletion.

steps.websiteResponse: The website permanently deletes the widget and its content, compacts the order of remaining widgets, shows Saving then Saved, updates lastEditedAt, and shows the editor without the widget.

alternatives.condition: The user cancels.

steps.websiteResponse: The website closes the confirmation and shows the widget unchanged.

alternatives.condition: The widget was already deleted.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the widget is already gone and shows the editor without it.

flows.outcome: Widget and its content permanently deleted, order of remaining widgets compacted, auto-saved and lastEditedAt refreshed; deletion survives refresh.

flows.name: Edit note widget text
flows.start: In the dashboard editor on a note widget
flows.goal: Type and edit plain text in a note widget.
preconditions: Dashboard open with at least one note widget.

steps.userAction: The user focuses the note text area in the note widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the note text field editable with the current plain text.

steps.userAction: The user types or edits the note text.
steps.websiteResponse: The website auto-saves the change with debounce, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

alternatives.condition: The note text is longer than 5000 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field, explains the 5000 character limit, and keeps what was typed without saving.

alternatives.condition: Auto-saving fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed text, shows that saving failed, and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The note widget was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the widget is gone and shows the editor without it.

flows.outcome: Note text updated, auto-saved with debounce and lastEditedAt refreshed; text survives refresh.

flows.name: Increase or decrease counter
flows.start: In the dashboard editor on a counter widget
flows.goal: Adjust the counter value by 1 and optionally set its label.
preconditions: Dashboard open with at least one counter widget.

steps.userAction: The user taps increase or decrease on the counter widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website changes the counter value by 1 (can go negative, starts at 0), shows the new number, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

steps.userAction: The user edits the counter label inline.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new label, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

alternatives.condition: The counter label is longer than 40 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the label field, explains the 40 character limit, and keeps what was typed without saving.

alternatives.condition: Saving the new counter value fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the previous value, shows that saving failed, and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: Saving the new label fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed label and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The counter widget was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the widget is gone and shows the editor without it.

flows.outcome: Counter value changed by +/-1 per click (can go negative, starts at 0) and Counter label optionally updated, auto-saved and lastEditedAt refreshed; value survives refresh.

flows.name: Manage checklist items
flows.start: In the dashboard editor on a checklist widget
flows.goal: Add, tick/untick, edit and remove tasks in a checklist.
preconditions: Dashboard open with at least one checklist widget.

steps.userAction: The user views the checklist widget items.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the ordered list of checklist items with text and checked state, or an empty state inviting to add the first item when there are none.

steps.userAction: The user adds a new item by filling the item text and submitting.
steps.websiteResponse: The website appends the item to the checklist in order, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

steps.userAction: The user ticks or unticks an item.
steps.websiteResponse: The website toggles the checked state for that item, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

steps.userAction: The user edits the text of an existing item inline and confirms.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the updated item text, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

steps.userAction: The user removes an item.
steps.websiteResponse: The website removes the item from the ordered list, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

alternatives.condition: The checklist has no items yet.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no items yet and invites the user to add the first item.

alternatives.condition: The item text is empty or longer than 120 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the item text field, explains that text is required and max 120 characters, and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving the new item fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed text and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The edited item text is empty or longer than 120 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field, explains the limit, and keeps what was typed without saving.

alternatives.condition: Saving the edited text fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed text and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: Saving the toggled state fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website restores the previous checked state, shows that saving failed, and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: Saving the removal fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the item in place, shows that saving failed, and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The checklist widget was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the widget is gone and shows the editor without it.

flows.outcome: Checklist items updated (added, checked state toggled, text edited, removed) in order, auto-saved and lastEditedAt refreshed; changes survive refresh.

flows.name: Manage link list items
flows.start: In the dashboard editor on a link list widget
flows.goal: Add, edit, remove and open links in a link list.
preconditions: Dashboard open with at least one link list widget.

steps.userAction: The user views the link list widget items.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the ordered list of links with title and URL, or an empty state inviting to add the first link when there are none.

steps.userAction: The user adds a new link by filling title and URL and submitting.
steps.websiteResponse: The website appends the link to the ordered list, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

steps.userAction: The user edits an existing link's title or URL and confirms.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the updated link, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

steps.userAction: The user removes a link.
steps.websiteResponse: The website removes the link from the ordered list, shows Saving then Saved, and updates lastEditedAt.

steps.userAction: The user clicks a link to open it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website opens the link's URL in a new tab.

alternatives.condition: The link list has no links yet.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no links yet and invites the user to add the first link.

alternatives.condition: The title is empty or longer than 80 characters, or the URL is empty or not a valid http:// or https:// URL.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that is wrong, explains that title is required max 80 and URL must be valid http/https, and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving the new link fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The edited title is empty or longer than 80 characters, or the edited URL is empty or not a valid http:// or https:// URL.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that is wrong, explains the requirement, and keeps what was typed without saving.

alternatives.condition: Saving the edited link fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: Saving the removal fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the link in place, shows that saving failed, and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The link list widget was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the widget is gone and shows the editor without it.

flows.outcome: Links updated (added, edited, removed) and can be opened in new tab; auto-saved and lastEditedAt refreshed; changes survive refresh.

flows.name: Manage account
flows.start: On any signed-in page via account menu
flows.goal: View my email and change my password.

steps.userAction: The user opens account settings.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the user's email read-only and the change password form.

steps.userAction: The user fills in current password and new password and submits the form.
steps.websiteResponse: The website verifies the current password, updates the password, keeps the session valid and shows confirmation that the password was changed.

alternatives.condition: The current password is empty or the new password is shorter than 8 characters or longer than 128 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that is wrong, explains what is required and keeps what was typed except it clears passwords for security.

alternatives.condition: The current password is incorrect.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the current password is incorrect and keeps the form values cleared for retry.

alternatives.condition: Updating the password fails.

steps.websiteResponse: The website keeps the values cleared and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: User sees their Email and can update Password; changes persist and survive refresh; session remains valid.

fields.label: Email
fields.meaning: Account email used to sign in and own dashboards

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: Secret protecting the account; new password when changing

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: How the user refers to the dashboard; required and shown in list and editor

fields.label: Title
fields.meaning: Optional heading for the widget; defaults to capitalized type name

fields.label: Type
fields.meaning: Kind of widget to add: note, counter, checklist or link list

fields.label: Note text
fields.meaning: Plain text content of a note widget

fields.label: Counter label
fields.meaning: Optional label describing what the counter counts

fields.label: Checklist item text
fields.meaning: Text of a single checklist item

fields.label: Link title
fields.meaning: Display title for a link in a link list widget

fields.label: Link URL
fields.meaning: Web address for the link; must be http or https

fields.label: Current password
fields.meaning: Existing password to verify identity before changing

assumptions.text: Home dashboard list doubles as browse and includes search by dashboard name (FD14) to satisfy the editor must-have browse/search expectation and P08 for lists that can grow to 50 dashboards; no additional filters or pagination beyond search in MVP
Editor is the view for dashboards; there is no separate read-only view. Interacting with widget content happens directly in the editor with auto-save
Widget create flow covers all four types via a type picker; type cannot be changed after creation, user must delete and re-add to change type
Account page shows email read-only and allows password change; email change and account deletion are out of scope for MVP

Publish, share, export, undo/redo and template/marketplace features are out of scope for MVP per outOfScope; no flows are provided for these acts beyond duplicate (F09) and widget reposition/resize/content acts
